Pluto sends its own emails through a **mail driver**. The first emails are the test email and the invitation. The driver is a contract, so a site can change the provider with no change to the rest of the site.

Core gives the contract, three drivers, two email templates, a server translator, and a guided setup page at **Settings, Email**.

## Configuration

All settings are private `runtimeConfig.plutoMail` values. An environment variable sets each one **at run time**. Do not put them in the build environment.

| Environment variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `NUXT_PLUTO_MAIL_DRIVER` | `resend`, `dev`, `none`, or the id of a registered driver. Empty means automatic. |
| `NUXT_PLUTO_MAIL_RESEND_API_KEY` | The Resend API key (`re_...`). |
| `NUXT_PLUTO_MAIL_FROM` | The From address, for example `Shop <hello@example.com>`. |
| `NUXT_PLUTO_MAIL_REPLY_TO` | The Reply-To address. Optional. |
| `NUXT_PLUTO_MAIL_MAILPIT_URL` | The URL of a Mailpit server, for example `http://localhost:8025`. Optional. |

Pluto keeps every secret in the environment. Nothing stores a key in the database, in the settings table, or in the GitHub CMS repository. A layer can register a secret store with `registerMailStore`. The environment always wins over a store.

## Choose the driver

Pluto picks the driver in this order:

1. `NUXT_PLUTO_MAIL_DRIVER`: a registered driver, or `resend`, `dev`, `none`. An unknown id gives `none` and logs one warning.
2. `resend`, when a Resend key resolves.
3. `dev`, in development.
4. `none`.

::warning
Production never falls back to the `dev` driver. A production site with no key has the `none` driver.
::

| Driver | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `resend` | Sends through the Resend HTTP API. |
| `dev` | In development, it prints the email to the server console, with the text version. You can copy an invite link from it. With `NUXT_PLUTO_MAIL_MAILPIT_URL`, it also posts the email to Mailpit. Outside development, it logs nothing. Without Mailpit, it throws `not_configured`. |
| `none` | Every send throws `not_configured`. The caller decides what to do. |

### The Resend driver

- It uses plain `fetch`, with no SDK.
- It sends a `User-Agent` header. Resend refuses a call without one.
- Each attempt has a 4 second timeout.
- Each send has an `Idempotency-Key`.
- It retries once with the same key, after a network error, a timeout, or a 5xx answer.
- With no From address, it uses `Pluto <onboarding@resend.dev>`. Resend delivers that address only to the email of the Resend account, until you verify a domain.

## Send an email

```ts
const email = await renderPlutoEmail('invite', { url, inviterName, roles }, { locale })
await sendPlutoMail({ to, ...email })
```

`sendPlutoMail` throws a `PlutoMailError` with a `code`:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `not_configured` | No driver can send. |
| `invalid_key` | Resend rejected the key. |
| `restricted_key` | The key is send-only and the call needs full access. |
| `test_sender_only` | The From domain is not verified. Resend sends only to the account owner. |
| `domain_not_verified` | The From domain is not verified. |
| `invalid_message` | The message or the request is not valid. A line break in a header value is also not valid. |
| `rate_limited`, `quota_exceeded` | Too many requests, or the plan limit is used. |
| `timeout`, `network`, `provider_error` | Resend did not answer, was not reachable, or failed. |

The error message is fixed English text. It never repeats the provider text, a recipient, a subject, a link, or a key. Mail code never logs these values. The one exception is the `dev` driver, which prints the email in development on purpose.

`sendPlutoMail` also refuses a message with no valid recipient. It refuses a subject, address, or Reply-To with a line break.

## Templates

An email template is a plain TypeScript function that returns `{ subject, html, text }`. There are two templates: `test` and `invite`. `renderPlutoEmail(name, data, { locale?, siteName? })` renders one.

- The texts are the `pluto.mail.*` keys of the locale files. An app can override them.
- The layout is a 600 px table with inline CSS, a button, and the plain link under it. It has a footer with the site name. It has no image and no tracking.
- Every text goes through `escapeHtml`. A button URL must be `http` or `https`.

## The server translator

`usePlutoServerTranslator(locale)` returns `{ t, te, tx, locale }` for a server route. It uses the same locale files as the admin. An unknown locale and a missing key fall back to the default locale.

## The Email settings page

**Settings, Email** is for administrators only. It is a guided flow.

A status card shows first: the driver, if a key is set, and the From address. Then seven steps:

1. Create a Resend account.
2. Add the API key. The page shows the line `NUXT_PLUTO_MAIL_RESEND_API_KEY=...` with a copy button. It checks if the key has full access or is send-only.
3. Send a test email to yourself. It works before you verify a domain, with the Resend test sender.
4. Add a domain. Enter the name and the region. The page shows the DNS records with copy buttons. **Verify** asks Resend to check. The page then checks the status every 10 seconds, then slower up to 60 seconds. It stops after 10 minutes. **Check again** starts it again.
5. Set the From address, and an optional Reply-To. The page shows the `NUXT_PLUTO_MAIL_FROM` line to copy.
6. Send a test email to anyone.
7. Optional: make a send-only key for the domain, to replace the setup key.

### Add a section

A layer adds a section below the steps with `mailPanels`:

```ts
definePlutoExtension({
  id: 'supabase',
  mailPanels: [
    { id: 'auth-emails', title: 'supabase.mail.authEmails.title', component: AuthEmailsPanel }
  ]
})
```

`title` and `description` are a key or a literal. Register the component with `defineAsyncComponent`.

## Admin routes

All routes are under `/api/_pluto/mail/`. They are for administrators only.

| Route | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `GET status` | The driver, the From address, and if a key is set. It has no secret. |
| `POST test` | Sends the test email. The limit is 5 calls in 10 minutes for each admin. |
| `POST resend/check-key` | Checks the key. `full` lists the domains. `sending` means send-only. |
| `POST resend/domains` | Creates a domain and returns the DNS records. |
| `GET resend/domains/:id` | Reads a domain with its status and records. |
| `POST resend/domains/:id/verify` | Asks Resend to check the DNS now. |
| `POST resend/sending-key` | Makes a send-only key. It returns the new key once. |

- The routes fail closed. They call `adapter.authorize(event, '*')`. With no content adapter, with an adapter that has no `authorize`, or when `authorize` throws, the answer is 403.
- A route that changes state also refuses a cross-site request.
- Keys never reach the browser. The one key in a response is the new send-only key, shown once.
- The test email limit is in memory, so each server instance counts for itself.

## Add a mail driver

See [Add a mail driver](/guides/add-a-mail-driver).

## Limits

- Pluto keeps the Resend key in the environment only. No layer ships a vault store yet.
- Only Resend has a guided setup. Another provider needs its own driver.
- Supabase sign-up, password reset, and magic link emails still go through the Supabase mailer. See [Invites and email](/supabase/invites-and-email).
